4. Pair each failure with a nearby success
This is the fastest way to see what changed.
For example:
failed: 1000228-10-K-2020.txt
success: 1000228-10-K-2019.txt
failed: 1000623-10-K-2020.txt
success: 1000623-10-K-2019.txt
failed: 1001233-10-K-2020.txt
success: 1001233-10-K-2019.txt
failed: 1000230-10-K-2021.txt
success: 1000230-10-K-2020.txt
That comparison will show whether the issue is:
heading wording changed
HTML parsing collapsed the heading incorrectly
heading exists only in anchor/name attributes
section title is present without “Item 1” or “Item 7”

library(data.table)

p <- fread("/Users/piomedolla/Desktop/effect-of-genai/cache/logs/extraction_progress.csv")

inspect_priority <- rbindlist(list(
  p[bus_status == "no_section_found" & mgmt_status == "no_section_found" & year >= 2020,
    .(priority = "both_missing_recent", row_id, cik, year, raw_file)],
  
  p[bus_status == "no_section_found" & mgmt_status == "ok",

  p[bus_status == "ok" & mgmt_status == "no_section_found",
    .(priority = "mgmt_missing_only", row_id, cik, year, raw_file)],
  
  p[overall_status == "done" & year >= 2019,
    .(priority = "recent_success_control", row_id, cik, year, raw_file)]

  order(priority, cik, year)
]

6. Even better: a matched failed/success control set
This is the most useful diagnostic file:
library(data.table)

p <- fread("/Users/piomedolla/Desktop/effect-of-genai/cache/logs/extraction_progress.csv")

failed_recent <- p[
  overall_status == "done_with_missing" & year >= 2020,
  .(cik, failed_year = year, failed_row_id = row_id, failed_raw = raw_file,
    bus_status, mgmt_status)
]

success_controls <- p[
  overall_status == "done",
  .(cik, success_year = year, success_row_id = row_id, success_raw = raw_file)
]

matched <- success_controls[
  failed_recent,
  on = .(cik)
][
  success_year == failed_year - 1L | success_year == failed_year - 2L
][
  order(cik, failed_year, -success_year)
]

fwrite(
  matched,
  "/Users/piomedolla/Desktop/effect-of-genai/cache/logs/failed_vs_success_controls.csv"
)

matched
7. What this likely means already
From your table, I would bet on three concrete extractor gaps:
For Business:
headings like OUR BUSINESS or just BUSINESS without ITEM 1
headings where ITEM 1 and BUSINESS are split across separate parsed nodes
headings embedded in anchors or table cells where normalization is over-collapsing structure
For MD&A:
headings like Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations where apostrophes/entities/tables split the phrase
Item 7 appearing only as ITEM 7. and the actual title on the next line
Item 7A or Item 8 boundary not being detected correctly after normalization
For both missing:
parsed text probably loses heading boundaries altogether after normalize_filing_text(f.text) because that function is flattening the vector too aggressively
That last point is important: in both extractors, doing this:
f.text <- normalize_filing_text(f.text)
after already extracting text nodes may be hurting you, because it is flattening heading structure line by line. That is a prime suspect.
